clue.text: Trio roaming around front of cattery restricted by whimsical behaviour of tigers?

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so the earlier letters sit inside

parts.note: fey means whimsical or otherworldly

indicators.note: around says the shuffled trio letters wrap the next piece
roaming means wandering about, so the letters of trio are rearranged
the front of a word is its first letter, here of cattery

explanation.surface: A cat lover muses on the wild, whimsical temperament of big cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whimsical' reads as describing tigers but supplies the outer letters; 'roaming' shuffles the trio and 'restricted by' means held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers are known for savage fierceness, so their behaviour illustrates the noun by example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Move quickly to acquire a couple of books with a pot?

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so the letters go inside

parts.note: to fly is to move quickly
B is short for book, so two of them

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to buy two books along with a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' looks like a vessel but means a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a pot belly means being soft and paunchy, so a flabby person might have one.

clue.text: Take in turn a tutorial principally engaged in traditional learning method

indicators.note: engaged in means locked inside, so these letters sit within the learning method

parts.note: learning by rote is memorising by repetition

indicators.note: principally means first, so the opening letter of tutorial

explanation.surface: A tutorial sits mainly within an old-fashioned teaching method.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate or swap duties on a regular cycle is to take them in turn.

clue.text: Singer but not a soprano, leading lady, one normally greeted?

explanation.walkthrough: 'leading lady' looks like an opera role but is the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor at the door is usually welcomed when they arrive, so it is someone normally greeted.

clue.text: Group of workers following excellent end to holiday getting possibly very short of energy and confused

indicators.note: following means the workers come after the earlier pieces

parts.note: tops means the best, excellent

parts.note: TU is a trade union

short of means without, so the energy letter is removed

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A union gets a great end to the holiday but very little energy and is muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: VERY without E is VRY; 'possibly' rearranges it to RVY.
explanation.definitionFit: Upside down and in disarray describes a confused, chaotic state.

clue.text: Run first of journals for society — producing a memorable number?

parts.note: in cricket a single is one run

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of journals

explanation.surface: An editor plans a run of journals for a society, hoping to produce a memorable issue.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE is one run in cricket; J replaces its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy advertising tune is a memorable piece of music, a number in the musical sense.

clue.text: Where one might find Cockney nits vaguely present?

definitions.text: Where one might find Cockney nits
definitions.meaning: nits live in hair, which a Cockney pronounces without its H
something sensed but not definite is present in the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A Cockney's head lice are somehow there.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop their aitches, so the place for nits sounds the same as the phrase meaning vaguely around.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour or feeling that is sensed around everyone without being pinned down is vaguely present.

clue.text: Bit of mail from relative lodging in grand rental property

an aunt is a relative

explanation.walkthrough: 'mail' looks like post but is chain mail; this is an armoured glove.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured glove was part of a knight's chain or plate armour, so it is a piece of armour.

clue.text: Work for schoolboy, perhaps, in trouble

definitions.meaning: a task set in class for practice

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of practice schoolwork is a classic task set, and to worry someone is an old sense of the verb.

clue.text: Retired European invested in stake for animal

explanation.definitionFit: An African grazing ruminant with horns is one kind of animal; the definition is a broad category.

clue.text: Head's turned and in luck when female's out to harmonise

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the shortened word for luck
out says the female letter is dropped from the word for luck

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone's head is turned and they're lucky once a woman leaves, so they get in tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is slang nut; 'turned' reads it backwards, 'out' drops the female letter and 'in' places one piece within the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring instruments or ideas into tune is to make them harmonise, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Report of extra unknown character in old Greek city short of sun incidentally

indicators.note: report of means the word is said aloud

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the ball being hit

short of means lacking, so the S is removed

parts.note: Thebes was a city of ancient Greece
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: A traveller reports some extra unknown feature of an ancient Greek city, as a passing remark.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not hit off the bat; 'Report of' makes it a sound-alike, 'short of' drops the sun and 'in' inserts the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in passing or by the way, used to introduce a side remark.

clue.text: Agitated short man cycling around city

cycling moves the last letter round to the front

explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like riding a bike but moves the end letter to the front; EC is the City of London, and 'around' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic and busy describes an agitated state, a synonym.

clue.text: Old car worker celebrating a notable achievement?

parts.note: Triumph was a British car maker
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.definitionFit: Exultant over a victory means rejoicing at success, a synonym.

clue.text: Irish family engaged in search snubbed by son showing peculiarity

kin are one's family

explanation.definitionFit: Oddness or eccentricity is the quality of being peculiar, a synonym.

clue.text: Fear Sikh militant is very unusual

clue.text: Rolling news — essentially old lot gets recycled

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Meeting and event with limitations exposed soured sadly? There's zero in it

clue.text: Ill-will beginning to mortify woman

clue.text: Scot, say, I found beside out-and-out place for pick-ups?
